judgments.title: Wong Teik Heng v TENAGA NASIONAL BERHAD
judgments.catchwords: 1. In Malaysia, electricity is ordinarily supplied and consumed before payment is made. The electricity meter is therefore more than a measuring device. It is the means by which electricity consumption is measured and translated into charges payable by the consumer. When a meter is tampered with or its proper recording of electricity consumption is interfered with, electricity may continue to be consumed without that consumption being accurately recorded. 2. The present dispute arises under the Electricity Supply Act 1990. Section 37 of the Electricity Supply Act 1990 creates offences relating, amongst others, to dishonest interference with or tampering of electricity meters and the dishonest prevention of such meters from duly recording electricity consumption. The Act also provides, under section 38, for the recovery by the licensee of loss of revenue arising from the relevant offences. 3. In particular, section 38(3) permits the licensee to require the consumer to pay for the loss of revenue due to an offence committed under section 37(1), (3) or (14), whilst section 38(5) provides for the recovery of the amount by civil action. 4. The present proceedings concern such a civil claim. The Respondent, as Plaintiff in the Sessions Court, sought to recover its alleged loss of revenue arising from the meter tampering. The Respondent was therefore required to establish its claim on a balance of probabilities. 5. The Respondent succeeded before the learned Sessions Court Judge. The learned Sessions Court Judge found, amongst others, that the Appellant was the registered consumer in respect of the relevant electricity supply and allowed the Respondent’s claim in the sum of RM697,164.75. 6. It is against that decision that the present appeal is brought.

judgments.title: TEOH SEW NGOH & ors v TEOH KHIAN GUAN
judgments.catchwords: 1. This is the Plaintiffs’ application in Enclosure 12 for discovery against the Defendant pursuant to Order 24 of the Rules of Court 2012. The parties are siblings, and the main dispute in these proceedings concerns the circumstances in which certain shares came to be registered in the Defendant’s name and whether he holds those shares on trust for the estate of their late mother. 2. The Plaintiffs seek discovery of various documents relating to the four companies concerned, the transfer of the disputed shares, the properties held by the said companies and the personal and/or joint bank accounts of the late Tan Sai Hong. 3. The documents sought include audited reports, management accounts, general ledgers, Forms 49, registers of members, share transfer forms, board and members’ resolutions, bank statements of the said companies, documents relating to the transfer of the properties and the personal and/or joint bank statements of the late Tan Sai Hong. 4. The Plaintiffs’ case is principally that the disputed shares were transferred or allotted to the Defendant through undue influence, dominion over the deceased, fraudulent calumny and/or in circumstances giving rise to non est factum. The Plaintiffs further allege that the Defendant holds the disputed shares on trust for the estate of the late Tan Sai Hong. 5. The Defendant disputes the Plaintiffs’ claim. He submits that the discovery sought is excessive and is not necessary for the fair disposal of the action or for saving costs. 6. Having considered the pleadings, affidavits and the written and oral submissions of the parties, this Court dismissed the application in Enclosure 12. These are the reasons for that decision.

judgments.title: Pendakwa Raya & ors v Julasiri Bin Akilmara
judgments.catchwords: Offence under section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 read together with section 34 of the Penal Code - Whether the trial judge should have informed at the close of the prosecution's case, that the defence was being called upon to answer a case of actual trafficking or presumed trafficking? - Overwhelming evidence proved the elements of custody, control, and knowledge - Actual possession of the impugned drugs was established - Section 180 (1) and (4) of the Criminal Procedure Code - Procedure after conclusion of case for prosecution - No statutory or legal requirement to state the presumption when calling for the defence - Formal verbal label for an evidentiary rule at the close of the prosecution's case is unnecessary - Statutory presumption of trafficking under section 37(da)(xvi) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 - Section 422 of the Criminal Procedure Code - Not vitiate the conviction - No miscarriage of justice - Failure either to make or to record such a finding does not ipso facto - The law does not require a mini-judgment or detailed legal reasons at the close of the prosecution’s case

judgments.title: MUHAMMAD HANIFF RAZRI BIN HASRI v Pendakwa Raya & ors
judgments.catchwords: Criminal Justice - Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, ss. 2, 37(d), 39B(1)(a) — Trafficking — Appeal against conviction — Whether statutory presumption of deemed possession under s. 37(d) can be conflated with substantive trafficking under s. 2 by "keeping and storing" without proof of an independent positive overt act beyond reasonable doubt — Presumption stacking and impermissible inversion of burden of proof — Criminal Procedure Code, s. 180(3) — Duty of trial court to amend charge to possession under s. 39A(2) where only s. 37(d) possession proved at close of prosecution case — Mid-trial mutation of case causing incurable prejudice and breach of natural justice — Evidence Act 1950, s. 54(1) — Prejudicial reception of bad character evidence (AADK document and smoking bong) — Break in chain of custody via non-contemporaneous, post-facto reconstruction of Drug Exhibit Register (POL 260) compromising identity of dangerous drugs — Non-exclusive access to ancestral premises and negative forensic nexus — Curative provisions inapplicable where foundational evidence of possession is fatally tainted — Conviction quashed and substituted conviction under s. 39A(2) refused — Accused acquitted and discharged.
coram: YA Datuk Wong Kian Kheong
YA Datuk Hayatul Akmal binti Abdul Aziz
YA Tuan Muniandy a/l Kannyappan
